about.title: El Cajon Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Work in El Cajon looks different from one block to the next. Auto shops and light industrial yards line E Main Street, retail and service jobs cluster along Broadway and Fletcher Parkway, and a good number of people spend their shift driving on I-8. When a workday ends in an injury, the first question is usually simple: who pays for this? In California, workers' compensation normally covers medical care and a portion of lost wages regardless of fault, and it is typically the only claim you can bring against your own employer. That is not always the whole story, though. If a subcontractor, a property owner, a defective piece of equipment, or another driver played a role in what happened, a separate third-party injury claim may exist alongside your comp benefits. We handle workplace injury claims on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why El Cajon Workers Choose Us

items.title: Two Claims, Not One
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually the only claim against your employer, but a negligent third party such as a subcontractor, property owner, or equipment maker can open a separate injury claim. We can look at both.

items.title: Deadlines Are Not Optional
items.desc: You generally need to report a work injury to your employer within 30 days, and any third-party claim carries California's two-year filing deadline. Getting help early keeps those windows open.

items.title: Retaliation Is Illegal
items.desc: California law prohibits an employer from firing, demoting, or punishing you for reporting a work injury. If that is what you are worried about, we can explain your protections before you decide anything.

items.question: I was hurt in a crash on I-8 while driving for my employer. Is that a workers' comp case or a car accident case?
items.answer: It can be both. Because you were working, workers' compensation would typically apply for medical care and wage replacement regardless of who caused the collision. If another driver was at fault, that driver is a third party, and a separate injury claim against them may be available with a two-year deadline. El Cajon recorded 619 injury collisions in 2025, many on I-8, so this overlap comes up more than people expect.

items.question: Can I sue my employer directly for a workplace injury in California?
items.answer: In most situations, no. Workers' compensation is the exclusive remedy against your employer, even if the employer was careless. The exceptions are narrow, so the more practical question is usually whether someone other than your employer, like a subcontractor, property owner, or equipment manufacturer, contributed to the injury.

items.question: What does it cost to get a case review?
items.answer: Nothing. We handle workplace injury matters on contingency, which means we are paid only if there is a recovery, and the fee terms are explained to you before you agree to anything.
